name: Jaw contouring makeup (contour/highlight)

lead: Jaw contouring uses darker and lighter makeup to suggest a more defined jaw. It is the same shading idea used for cheekbones and noses.
It is temporary and works as an optical effect.

paras: Darker shades read as shadow and lighter shades as raised areas, changing perceived shape.
The sources consulted do not discuss risks.

lead: Jaw contouring is the use of makeup shading and highlighting to make the jawline look more defined. It applies the general technique of contouring, in which a shade darker than the skin creates apparent shadow and a lighter shade brings areas forward.[1]
The technique has a long theatrical and film history and became mainstream in the 2010s through celebrity and social media use.[1] It is temporary and cosmetic.
infobox: Contour and highlight powders or creams

paras: General contouring places a darker shade in hollows or along edges to suggest shadow and a lighter shade on prominent areas; strobing uses lighter shades only.[1] Applied to the jaw, the same shading principle is used to suggest a sharper edge. The reference article on contouring does not discuss the jawline specifically.[1]

Elizabethan actors used chalk and soot to be read from a distance, and greasepaint later replaced soot under electric lighting. Max Factor added shading to film faces in the studio era, and Kevyn Aucoin's 2000 book Face Forward is credited with introducing sculpting to the public. The 2010s Kardashian era made intense contouring widespread, and drag performers use it to emphasize or soften features.[1]

timeline.event: Max Factor Sr. reportedly presents an early face-contouring tutorial.[1]
Kevyn Aucoin publishes Face Forward, credited with popularizing sculpting.[1]
Celebrity use drives mainstream contour and strobing products.[1]
